concepts.title: Doctor Dolittle Becomes an Animal Doctor
concepts.section: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us read
concepts.definition: A stomach-ached visitor and a wise parrot convince John Dolittle that his true gift is with animals; he learns their languages, gives up his people's practice, and becomes the most famous animal doctor in the world.
concepts.key_idea: A career changes when talent meets need: Dolittle knows animals so well that treating them is the natural work for him.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr102.txt, Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us read

solution_steps.explain: Retell what happens in one or two sentences with the main character named.
Point to the moment of change or the idea the text keeps returning to.
Say the message of the text in one clear sentence of your own.

concepts.title: Polynesia: Teacher of Bird Language
concepts.section: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us read I
concepts.definition: Polynesia the parrot speaks both people's language and bird language; she insists animals can talk, gives the Doctor the Birds' A.B.C., and explains that animals also speak with ears, feet and tails.
concepts.key_idea: A good teacher opens a hidden world; Polynesia's patient word-by-word lessons turn doubt into skill.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr102.txt, Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us read I

solution_steps.explain: List what the character does and says at the key moments.
Match each action to a quality such as courage, kindness or curiosity.
Point to the exact lines of the text that support each trait.

concepts.title: Listening to Animals: The Horse's Lesson
concepts.section: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us read II
concepts.definition: The plough horse shows why animal patients suffer: vets give pills without asking, because animals cannot complain. Able to talk with the horse at last, Dolittle learns the real trouble is failing eyesight and orders green spectacles.
concepts.key_idea: Right treatment starts with listening; the horse's complaint that anyone thinks he can doctor animals is the heart of the story.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr102.txt, Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us read II
question_patterns: what was the real problem of the plough horse

solution_steps.explain: Note what the horse says is wrong and what the earlier vet had done.
Check that spectacles, not pills, answer the real need.
State why listening matters in every kind of doctoring.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Scholar, Cellar and Countryside
concepts.section: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Story words grow from context: a scholar is a learned person, a cellar is a room below ground level, and the countryside is the rural area around a town.
concepts.key_idea: Place words like cellar and countryside map the little house at Puddleby where the animals crowd in.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr102.txt, Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us learn
question_patterns: what does scholar mean in this chapter

solution_steps.explain: Find the sentence in which the new word appears.
Use the words before and after to sense what meaning fits.
Swap in the guessed meaning; if the sentence still works, it is right.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why were farm animals seen wearing glasses around Puddleby?

solution_template.explain: The plough horse admitted to failing eyesight once someone could understand him.
Other animals told their friends about the talking doctor, so green spectacles became the norm in the countryside.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What advice does Polynesia give the Doctor after the visitor leaves?

solution_template.explain: The Cat's-food-Man says Dolittle knows animals better than the local vets.
Polynesia tells him to give up silly people and take care of animals, who will soon recognise his worth.
